Bathroom

Tape this page inside the cabinet door

🩷 Pink Cloths

🩷Cloth A: Toilet only
Seat, lid, handle, base
🩷Cloth B: Everything else
Sink, counter, taps, mirror
Every day: use one clean Cloth A and one clean Cloth B.
Wash the used cloths daily, so a clean set is always ready.
Daily every day

Tidy the area first

  1. Clear the counter and any surfaces of personal items, toiletries, and clutter
  2. Set them aside in a basket or tray, somewhere out of the way, not just onto another surface

Wipe mirror

  1. Spray the glass cleaner
  2. Wipe with the general cloth (or a paper towel): circular motions for large mirrors, side-to-side for narrow ones, until it looks clean, with no streaks
  3. If the cloth gets too damp, flip to a dry side or fold to a fresh section

Wipe down the cabinet doors

  1. Spray the general cloth (not the doors directly) with Dettol Antibacterial Surface Cleanser
  2. Wipe both cabinet doors under the sink, front and sides, top to bottom
  3. Dry with a clean cloth so no streaks or water spots are left on the gloss finish
Dettol Antibacterial Surface Cleanser (Lime)Non-bleach, safe on most surfaces

Wipe down taps & stainless steel

  1. Wet the general cloth with warm water. Add 1 small drop of dish soap directly onto the cloth (not the tap) and wipe the taps
  2. Wipe again with a second clean damp cloth (no soap) to rinse off residue
  3. Dry with a dry cloth or paper towel, no water spots left behind
Note: check every 2–4 weeks, only treat if you actually see white/cloudy mineral spots. Natural option: wrap a cloth soaked in white vinegar or lemon juice around the tap for 1–3 hours, then rinse. Or use the descaler spray: leave 1–2 min, wipe, rinse well. Never mix vinegar/descaler with bleach.
Limescale/descaler spray (acidic), or natural: vinegar/lemonFor occasional mineral buildup only, not daily
Natural Descaling Method (Lemon & Vinegar) for Occasional Buildup

Clean shower/tub

Wear gloves for this task
  1. Clear shampoo bottles and anything else out of the way first
  2. Spray the mold & mildew remover on walls, tub floor, and grout lines
  3. Let it sit 5–10 minutes, no scrubbing needed for light buildup
  4. Rinse well with water
  5. Wipe the shower head, mixer/taps, and drain cover: wet the cloth with warm water, add 1 small drop of dish soap directly onto the cloth (not the fixture), wipe, then use a second clean damp cloth (no soap) to rinse off residue
  6. Dry everything, including the stainless steel, with a cloth to prevent water spots and help prevent new mold growth
Note: open a window or the door while using this, it's bleach-based, so ventilate the room. Never use toilet bowl cleaner on the shower/tub, it's too strong and can permanently damage the surface. Never spray the mold & mildew remover directly onto the shower head, mixer/taps, or any stainless steel, the bleach dulls the surface over time; clean those separately with the dish soap method above.

Clean the toilet

Wear gloves for this task
  1. Dust the toilet first, top to bottom down to the base, with toilet paper or a dry cloth, before spraying anything wet. This stops dust and hair turning into a sticky mess
  2. Squirt cleaner under the rim in a full circle
  3. Scrub inside the bowl and around the base with the toilet brush
  4. Let the cleaner sit at least 5 minutes before flushing
  5. Flush
  6. Wipe the seat, lid, handle & base with the toilet-only cloth
  7. Wipe behind the toilet, around the base where it meets the floor, and the tank/cistern lid at the back. These spots get missed and collect dust and grime
  8. Rinse the toilet brush under the flush water, spray it with disinfectant (vinegar, hydrogen peroxide, or the toilet cleaner itself), then stand it upright/open to air dry. Never shut it wet into a closed holder, it breeds bacteria

Mop floor: always last

The mop only cleans if it stays clean. A dirty mop doesn’t wipe dirt away, it just spreads the same dirty water around the floor. Rinse it often, not just at the end.
  1. Sweep first, all loose dirt and hair off the floor
  2. Fill the mop bucket about halfway with warm water (roughly 4 liters)
  3. Add 1 tablespoon of dish soap (about 1 capful of the bottle) and stir to mix. (No dish soap yet? Use 1 tablespoon of the antibacterial spray liquid instead, same amount)
  4. Dip the mop, then squeeze it out well. It should feel damp, not dripping
  5. Start in the corner farthest from the door. Work one small section at a time, about 1 meter by 1 meter
  6. On each section, go over it 2–3 times with S-shaped strokes, pressing down. One quick swipe is not enough, you're lifting dirt off the floor, not just wetting it
  7. After every 2–3 sections, rinse the mop: swish it in the bucket water, squeeze it out again, then keep going. Do this the whole time, not just when you remember
  8. As soon as the bucket water looks cloudy, grey, or dirty, stop and change it. Empty the bucket, refill with clean water + soap, then continue. Never keep mopping with dirty water, it just spreads the dirt back onto the floor
  9. Work backward section by section toward the door, so you never step on the floor you've already cleaned
  10. Once the whole floor is done, empty the bucket and refill with plain water, no soap. Go over the entire floor a second time with this clean water. This rinse pass is what actually leaves it clean, not sticky or streaky
  11. Let air dry
Note: weekly optional deep clean, fill the bucket with 4 liters of warm water, add ½ cup (120ml) white vinegar, stir. Mop, then go over once more with a mop dipped in plain water to rinse. Never full-strength, and never daily, frequent vinegar damages grout over time.
SWIPE 紅威寶 Super Concentrate Dishwashing Detergent (Original), or antibacterial spray (diluted)No dedicated floor cleaner needed

Put all products away

After cleaning, return every bottle, spray, and cloth to its storage spot, nothing left out on the counter, floor, or edge of the tub.

Every 3 Days not daily

Fresh towels & bath mat

  1. Swap for clean, dry towels every 3 days, not daily
  2. Every time you change the towels, also swap the bath mat for a clean one. White only, like the one in the photo
Weekly once a week

Deep-clean toilet brush & holder

Wear gloves for this task
  1. Soak the brush head in the toilet bowl with the toilet cleaner, OR mix your own: ⅓ cup (80ml) bleach into 4 liters of water in a bucket (3% hydrogen peroxide, undiluted, is a non-bleach alternative). Either way, soak for 30–60 minutes
  2. Scrub
  3. Rinse well
  4. Air dry fully upright
  5. Wash the holder tray with disinfectant too, it collects dirty water and breeds bacteria too
Note: if mixing bleach yourself, make a fresh batch each time, it loses strength after 24 hours. Keep it on the brush for at least 1 minute before scrubbing. If your household leaves the toilet lid down, don't leave the brush soaking in the bowl overnight, it's an unpleasant surprise for the next person.
Clorox Toilet Bowl Cleaner Bleach (Lemon), diluted bleach, or 3% hydrogen peroxideNon-bleach option: hydrogen peroxide

Clean the drains (sink + shower)

Wear gloves for this task
  1. Remove the drain cover or stopper if removable
  2. Pull out any visible hair and debris
  3. Pour a kettle of hot water down each drain to clear soap residue
  4. If draining slowly, use a drain-safe cleaner following the label, or a mix of baking soda and hot water
Note: this prevents clogs and the musty smell that builds up in drains over time.
Lion Tung Kui Lou (獅王通渠佬) Drain CleanerUse if slow-draining, follow the bottle’s instructions
Monthly once a month

Clear out & wipe under-sink and mirror cabinet shelves

  1. Take everything out of the cabinet under the sink and the cabinet behind the mirror
  2. Spray each shelf with the Dettol Antibacterial Surface Cleanser (same bottle used for the sink & counter)
  3. Wipe every shelf dry
  4. Put everything back neatly
Dettol Antibacterial Surface Cleanser (Lime)Non-bleach, safe on most surfaces
Never Mix These Products
Bleach products Toilet bowl cleaner, mold & mildew remover
✕
Acid descaler Limescale spray for taps

Mixing bleach and an acid descaler makes toxic gas. Never use both at once, in the same bucket, or on the same cloth. Rinse one away fully and let it dry before switching to the other. Wear gloves whenever you use either one.
